title: Is Caterpillar a Sneaky Good AI Stock to Buy Right Now? | CAT Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks whether Caterpillar is a buying opportunity after crashing from about $1,000 to about $600. He recommended it as a buy as far back as 2023 but warned investors to take profits above $750, and has said since then it was not a buying opportunity. The old slow-growing dividend stock has been transformed by AI: its power-generation business for data centres is booming, with orders out to 2029 and capacity set to more than triple by 2030, plus autonomous equipment solutions as a second growth source. Management reiterated almost 20% revenue growth this year, but inflation and tariff-driven import costs are squeezing free cash flow to the low end of target as the company absorbs those costs. Even so, margins sit near decade highs (19% cash flow from operations, 18% operating margin) and Wall Street expects over 18% EPS growth for several years. Forward P/E of 18.5 roughly matches EPS growth at a 1:1 ratio. He revised his DCF valuation significantly higher to $531 per share versus about $597 now, so the stock looks fairly valued to slightly overvalued — not a buy yet, but 'another 10 or 15% down and I can see myself upgrading Caterpillar stock to a buy'. Note: the caption file ends mid-sentence, so the closing line is cut off. Calls: CAT CONDITIONAL_BUY at about $507-537 (first tracked).
